findings.title: Null-check verifies grantType twice, not rawTokenId
findings.body: The AccessTokenContext constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) and then Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null raw token id is therefore accepted. encodeTokenId later concatenates it, so the jti becomes a string ending in ":null" rather than failing fast, and any later lookup or event correlation using that id is wrong.

findings.title: Access-token id matcher checks the wrong slice and inverts the grant check
findings.body: isAccessTokenId is what CODE_TO_TOKEN, refresh, device, and CIBA event assertions now use for Details.TOKEN_ID. Encoded ids are session(2) + tokenType(2) + grant(2) + ':' + uuid, so the grant shortcut is substring(4, 6). The matcher uses substring(3, 5) (last character of the token-type shortcut plus the first grant character) and returns false when that slice equals the expected shortcut. For a normal id such as onrtac:<uuid> the slice is "ta", which is not "ac", so the condition does not fail and only the UUID half is checked. Tests therefore pass even if the grant (or the whole prefix) is wrong, and a prefix shorter than 5 characters throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of a matcher mismatch.

findings.title: getShortcut is abstract, documented as 3 letters, and never length-checked
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() was added with no default, so every existing custom grant factory fails with AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls it, which prevents server startup. The javadoc says the shortcut is usually 3 letters, but the encoder requires exactly 2 characters: encodeTokenId concatenates the shortcut as-is, and getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects any prefix whose length is not 6. A grant that follows the javadoc (or returns any non-2-character shortcut) will issue access tokens that cannot be decoded, and postInit only compares map sizes, so it does not reject a bad length before those tokens are minted.

findings.title: Duplicate grant shortcuts are not reliably rejected
findings.body: postInit inserts every grant shortcut into grantsByShortcuts without checking that the shortcut is unique or exactly two characters, then only compares the two map sizes. That comparison misses the case where a shortcut collision is paired with an id collision (both maps shrink by the same amount) and is not repeated on the lazy refresh path in getShortcutByGrantType / getGrantTypeByShortcut. A colliding shortcut silently overwrites the other grant, so a token can be encoded as one grant and decoded as another, which breaks the session-lookup and token-exchange optimizations this id format is meant to support.
